text: The retrieved literature that bears on the study's hypothesis is thin. Van Bavel et al. (2020) argue that social and behavioural science can inform the COVID-19 pandemic response, which gives general support to testing whether short messages shift public attitudes toward science. Lewandowsky et al. (2017) examine how misinformation affects people and how it can be countered, which is the closest match to a message-versus-control design on trust. Berinsky et al. (2012) assess the internal and external validity of experiments run on Amazon Mechanical Turk, a relevant consideration for an online message experiment of this kind. The retrieved works do not directly test whether messages change trust in science, so there is no clear finding for or against the hypothesis. The main tension is between Lewandowsky et al. (2017), who stress the adverse influence of misinformation and the difficulty of countering it, and the more general optimism of Van Bavel et al. (2020) about behavioural interventions. A relative-to-control design of the kind the study uses can test whether any message moves trust above the pure control.
